title: Grade 11 Geography National Exam & Practice 2024 (8 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 8 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the most widely supported scientific theory regarding the origin of the Universe and the Earth?
questions.explanation:
The Big Bang Theory is the most widely supported scientific model explaining that the Universe originated from an abrupt cosmic explosion and expansion of matter 10–20 billion years ago,

 which eventually led to the formation of stars, planets, and other space objects, including the Earth.

questions.questionText: Approximately how many years ago was the Earth formed from a mixture of gas and dust particles moving around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Our Earth was created from the mixture of gas and dust particles moving in space around the Sun about 4.5 billion years ago.

questions.questionText: The initial land masses on Earth gathered to form an early supercontinent known as Rodinia. In which geological timescale did Rodinia exist?
questions.explanation: The early continent called 'Rodinia' formed at about 750 Ma, during the Neoproterozoic Supercontinent period.

questions.questionText: The breakup of the supercontinent Pangaea is believed to have begun during which geological period?
questions.explanation: Pangaea came into being at about 255 -210 Ma, and started to break apart from 210 -180 Ma, which corresponds to the Triassic period.

questions.questionText: The concept that the continents are slowly moving across the Earth's surface is known as:
questions.explanation: Continental drift is the large-scale movement of continents across the Earth's surface over geological time.

questions.questionText: What was the name of the supercontinent that evolved around the South Pole during the late Cambrian period (514 Ma)?
questions.explanation: During the late Cambrian period (514 Ma) the Gondwana Supercontinent had evolved around the South Pole.

questions.questionText: The collision of the Laurasia continent with the Baltica continent closed the Iapetus Sea during the mid-Silurian Period (425 Ma). This continuous collision led to the formation of which geological mass?
questions.explanation: The continual collision that closed the Iapetus Sea during the mid-Silurian had then produced the pre-Pangaea continent during the early Devonian period, at about 390 Ma.

questions.questionText: Which geological era is commonly referred to as the 'age of ancient life' and marked the beginning of life with common species like trilobites and shelled animals?
questions.explanation: The Paleozoic era (600 to 250 Ma) is commonly referred to as the age of ancient life, and it marked the beginning of life with trilobites and shelled animals as common species.

questions.questionText: The Devonian period, the fourth period of the Paleozoic era, is often referred to as the:
questions.explanation: The Devonian, the fourth period of the Paleozoic, was rich in fish species and referred to as the age of fish.

questions.questionText: The mass extinction of Earth species at the end of the Paleozoic era was primarily caused by:
options: The formation of the supercontinent Pangaea
questions.explanation: The creation of Pangaea at the end of the Paleozoic era led to extreme seasonal weather changes that caused the great extinction of Earth species.

questions.questionText: Which geological era is best known as the 'age of Dinosaurs'?
questions.explanation: The Mesozoic era (250-70 Ma) is often referred to as the era of middle life and the age of Dinosaurs owing to their relative dominance.

questions.questionText: During the mid-Mesozoic era, the splitting of Pangaea resulted in the formation of two major landmasses. What were these landmasses called?
questions.explanation: The mid-Mesozoic era was experiencing the splitting of Pangaea into Laurasia and Gondwanaland.

questions.questionText: The end of the Mesozoic era is most famously marked by which major event?
options: The formation of the supercontinent Pangaea
The beginning of life on Earth
The formation of the first birds
questions.explanation: The end of the Mesozoic era saw the emergence of land mammals but marked the mass extinction of Dinosaurs.

questions.questionText: Which geological era is the most recent one, covering the time since 70 Ma, and is commonly named the 'age of mammals'?
questions.explanation: The Cenozoic era is the recent one covering the time since 70 Ma, and is commonly named an era of recent life and the age of mammals, birds, and flowering plants.

questions.questionText: During the beginning of the Cenozoic era, the rifting of Pangaea was fully achieved, leading to which major geological outcome?
options: The formation of the Iapetus Sea
The continents retaining their present form
The dominance of trilobites and shelled animals
The emergence of the first Dinosaurs
questions.explanation: During the beginning of the Cenozoic era, the rifting of Pangaea has been fully achieved and the continents retained their present form.

questions.questionText: What term is used to describe the process of mountain formation, especially through the folding of the Earth's crust, which was experienced during the Cenozoic era?
questions.explanation:
Orogenic is the formation of mountains, especially through the folding of the Earth's crust.

Great volcanism and orogenic folding caused the formation of numerous volcanic, fault-block, and fold mountains in the different parts of the Earth’s continents during the Cenozoic era.

questions.questionText: What percentage of the Earth's surface area is covered by water (hydrosphere)?
questions.explanation: All water (hydrosphere) in total covers greater than 71% of Earth’s surface.

questions.questionText: Oceans account for what percentage of all the water on Earth?
questions.explanation: The largest bodies of water are the Oceans, which account for over 97% of all the water on Earth.

questions.questionText: In the Southern Hemisphere, the ratio of land to ocean is approximately:
questions.explanation:
The distribution of Ocean basins and Continents is unevenly arranged.

The ratio of land to ocean is about 1:1.5 in the Northern Hemisphere, but it is 1:4 in the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.questionText: Which hemisphere experiences a more moderate climate due to the greater abundance of water and the ocean's ability to release large amounts of stored heat energy?
questions.explanation: The greater abundance of water in the Southern Hemisphere causes its climate to tend to be more moderate because of the ocean's ability to release large amounts of stored heat energy.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the largest continent in the world, covering one-third of the total land area of the Earth?
questions.explanation:
Asia is the largest continent in the world.

It lies in the eastern hemisphere covering one-third of the total land area of the earth.

questions.questionText: Which is the only continent in the world that is crossed by the Equator, the Tropic of Cancer, and the Tropic of Capricorn?
questions.explanation: Africa is the only continent in the world crossed by the equator, Tropic of Cancer, and Tropic of Capricorn.

questions.questionText: The world's largest hot desert (Sahara) and the world's longest river (River Nile) are both found on which continent?
questions.explanation: The world’s largest hot desert (Sahara), and the world’s longest river (River Nile), are found in Africa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is often called an 'Island continent' or 'Oceania' and is the smallest continent in the world?
questions.explanation:
Australia is the smallest continent in the world.

It is surrounded by water on all of its sides and often called an Island continent or Oceania.

questions.questionText: Which continent is a permanently ice-covered landmass located around the South Pole, and is the third smallest continent on Earth?
questions.explanation:
Antarctica is a permanently ice covered continent located around the South-Pole.

It is the third smallest continent on the earth.

questions.questionText: Europe is the second smallest continent in the world. From which mountain range is it separated from Asia?
questions.explanation: Asia is separated by the Ural Mountains from Europe, making them part of the Eurasia landmass.

questions.questionText: North America is linked to South America by a narrow strip of land known as the:
questions.explanation: North America is linked to South America by the narrow strip of land called the Isthmus of Panama.

questions.questionText: The world's largest river (Amazon River), the largest and most bio-diverse rainforest, and the longest north-south extending mountain range (Andes Mt.) are all found in:
questions.explanation: The world’s largest River (Amazon River), largest and most bio-diverse rainforest, and the north-south extending longest mountain (Andes Mt.) are found in South America.

questions.questionText: By area, which is the world's largest ocean basin, covering 28% of the Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is by far the world’s largest ocean basin with about 155,557,000 square kilometers, covering 28% of the Earth.

questions.questionText: What is the deepest point in the world, which is located in the Pacific Ocean basin?
questions.explanation: The deepest point in the Pacific Ocean is the Challenger Deep within the Mariana Trench, about 10,924 meters deep, which is also the deepest point in the world.

questions.questionText: Which ocean basin is the world's second-largest and contains the majority of the Earth’s shallow Seas, such as the Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of Mexico?
questions.explanation:
The Atlantic Ocean is the world’s second-largest Ocean (76,762,000 square kilometers).

It contains the majority of the Earth’s shallow Seas, including the Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and Mediterranean Sea.

questions.questionText: The Indian Ocean is known for causing which major weather patterns that dominate much of Southeast Asia?
options: El Niño and La Niña cycles
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean is known for causing the monsoon weather patterns that dominate much of Southeast Asia.

questions.questionText: Which ocean is the world’s smallest ocean (14,056,000 square kilometers) and is largely covered by a drifting polar icepack throughout most of the year?
questions.explanation:
The Arctic Ocean is the world’s smallest Ocean with an area of 14,056,000 square kilometers.

Throughout most of the year, much of it is covered by a drifting polar icepack.

questions.questionText: The Southern Ocean was delimited as the fifth ocean in the spring of 2000 by the International Hydrographic Organization. What is its southern boundary?
options: The coast of Antarctica to 60 degrees south latitude
questions.explanation: The Southern Ocean extends from the coast of Antarctica to 60 degrees south latitude, delimited by the International Hydrographic Organization in 2000.

questions.questionText: Which trench represents the deepest point in the Atlantic Ocean basin?
questions.explanation: The deepest point of the Atlantic Ocean is the Puerto Rico Trench, which is some 8,605 meters deep.

questions.questionText: The Paleozoic era ended with the formation of the supercontinent Pangaea. The era itself covered the time period from:
questions.explanation: The Paleozoic era covered the time from 600 to 250 Ma from the present.

questions.questionText: The term for the development stages of the Earth's continents and their relative position/distribution over geological times is studied under:
questions.explanation: The development stages of the Earth's continents and their relative position are the main contents of the unit 'Formation of the Continents'.

questions.questionText: What is the collective term for a large area of land mostly separated by a water body?
questions.explanation: A continent is a huge area of land mostly separate by a water body.

questions.questionText: Which of the following processes widened the continental cracks, leading to the creation of bigger water masses (Oceans) during the late Cretaceous Period?
questions.explanation: During the late Cretaceous, the breaking-apart of Pangaea widened and bigger water masses (Oceans) were created along the continental cracks.

questions.questionText: The formation of the first mammals and the first Dinosaurs occurred during which geological period, marked by the start of the Pangaea break-up?
questions.explanation: The Triassic period (208 - 250 Ma) is associated with the start of the Pangaea break-up and the emergence of the first mammals and first Dinosaurs.

questions.questionText: The formation of the first birds is generally associated with which period of the Mesozoic era?
questions.explanation: The Cretaceous period (70 - 144 Ma) is listed in the geological timescale as the time for the first birds.

questions.questionText: Modern humans appeared during which epoch of the Quaternary period?
questions.explanation: The Holocene epoch (Present – 0.01 Ma) is the time when Modern Humans appeared.

questions.questionText: The Earth's continents reached their present position during which geological epoch/period?
questions.explanation: Continental break-up progressively continued during the Tertiary period; the Earth’s continents have then retained their present position during the Quaternary period.

questions.questionText: What term refers to the major features of the Earth's surface that are formed due to the Earth's movement of crustal plates?
questions.explanation: The major landforms (continents and oceanic) are formed due to the earth’s movement of crustal plates (see Unit One).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven known continents on the Earth today?
questions.explanation:
The seven known continents are Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America.

Eurasia is a major landmass but not counted as a separate continent in this list, though Asia and Europe are part of it.

questions.questionText: The Iapetus Sea was closed during the mid-Silurian Period due to the collision between which two continents?
questions.explanation: The Laurasia continent collided with the Baltica and closed the Iapetus Sea during the mid-Silurian (425 Ma).

questions.questionText: Which keyword is NOT explicitly listed in the main content of Unit 1, although it is a related concept for the changing positions of continents?
questions.explanation:
The keywords explicitly listed for sections 1.1 and 1.4 are Big bang, Pangaea, Continents, Rodinia, Continental drift, Sea-floor spreading, mid-oceanic, Solar system, and Oceans.

While Plate tectonics is mentioned in related content (like the cause of major landforms), it is not listed as a primary keyword for the changing position section as Continental drift is[cite: 40, 202, 348].

questions.questionText: The total surface area of the Earth is estimated to be approximately:
questions.explanation: The surface area of the Earth is estimated to be 510,072,000 square kilometers.

questions.questionText: What percentage of the Earth's water is contained in glaciers and polar ice caps in the form of solid ice?
questions.explanation: Glaciers and polar ice caps contain just greater than 2% of the Earth’s water in the form of solid ice.

questions.questionText: Compared to water found in lakes, inland seas, and rivers, groundwater is about how much more plentiful beneath the surface?
questions.explanation: Groundwater is 36 times more plentiful than water found in lakes, inland Seas, rivers, and in the atmosphere as water vapor.

questions.questionText: The Arctic Circle crosses the northern margin of which two continents?
questions.explanation:
The Arctic Circle is mentioned to cross the northern margin of Asia and Europe , and the Arctic Ocean, which is found between Europe, Asia, and North America.

 The Arctic Ocean is bordered by North America and Asia, and the circle crosses them both.

questions.questionText: Which continent is the third largest on Earth and is surrounded by the Atlantic, Pacific, and Arctic Oceans?
questions.explanation:
North America is the third largest continent of the earth.

 It lies north of the equator in the western hemisphere and surrounded by the Atlantic, Pacific and Arctic Oceans.

questions.questionText: The deep depression known as the Dead Sea and the highest precipitation area (Assam) are major features found on which continent?
questions.explanation: Asia has the highest mountains (Himalayas), the deepest depressions (Dead Sea), the driest desert (Lut desert), highest precipitation (Assam) and long tradition of civilization (Mesopotamia).

questions.questionText: The maximum depth of the Indian Ocean is located at which feature?
options: Java Trench or Sunda Double Trench
questions.explanation: The deepest point of the Indian Ocean is at the Java Trench or Sunda Double Trench.

questions.questionText: Which ocean basin receives more freshwater from continental runoff than any other ocean basin, draining major rivers like the Amazon and Mississippi?
questions.explanation:
The Atlantic Ocean basin drains some of the world’s largest rivers including the Amazon and Mississippi.

It receives more freshwater from continental runoff than any other Ocean basin.

questions.questionText: What is the collective name given to the three periods: Paleocene, Eocene, and Oligocene?
questions.explanation: The Paleocene, Eocene, Oligocene, Miocene, and Pliocene epochs all fall under the Tertiary Period, which is a major division of the Cenozoic Era (The Paleogene and Neogene are the periods/sub-eras).

questions.questionText: The supercontinent that existed approximately 255 - 210 Ma, immediately before its major break-up, was:
questions.explanation: The Supercontinent (Pangaea) had come into being at about 255 -210 Ma.

questions.questionText: Which of the following epochs is the most recent, starting at 0.01 Ma?
questions.explanation: The Holocene epoch covers the time from Present – 0.01 Ma.

questions.questionText: The splitting of Pangaea widened, and North America moved away from which continent during the late Cretaceous period?
questions.explanation:
The break-up had continued until the late Cretaceous.

In the meantime, North America had moved away from the African continent.

questions.questionText: Which is the driest inhabited continent in the world, with 70 percent of its area classified as either arid or semi-arid?
questions.explanation: Australia is the driest inhabited continent in the world with 70 percent of it either arid or semi-arid.

questions.questionText: The total area of the Earth's oceans is estimated to be about:
questions.explanation: The area of the Oceans is about 363, 000,000 square kilometers.

questions.questionText: During the Cenozoic era, which type of life forms succeeded and became dominant on Earth?
questions.explanation: During the Cenozoic era, Birds, mammals, and flowering plants became dominant on Earth.

questions.questionText: The formation of the initial land masses to create the early continent 'Rodinia' is generally dated at about:
questions.explanation:
The first cosmic rocks solidified and created the first Earth at about 4600 to 3900 Ma.

Following that, initial land masses gathered to form the early continent called ‘Rodinia’.

questions.questionText: Which ocean has the warmest surface ocean temperatures due to its proximity to the equator?
questions.explanation: Because of its proximity to the equator, the Indian Ocean basin has the warmest surface Ocean temperatures.

questions.questionText: In which period did the four major continents (Gondwana, Baltica, Siberia, and Laurasia) come into being, following the Rodinia supercontinent?
questions.explanation: Next to the formation of Gondwana, four major continents (Gondwana, Baltica, Siberia, and Laurasia) came into being during 458 Ma (in the mid-Ordovician Period).

questions.questionText: Which sea is one of the shallow seas found in the Atlantic Ocean basin?
questions.explanation: The shallow Seas found in the Atlantic Ocean basin are the: Baltic Sea, Black Sea, Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, North Sea, and the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.questionText: The Mesozoic era is characterized by low-lying areas that were occasionally flooded by shallow marine transgressions, followed by depositions of:
questions.explanation: Low-lying areas were occasionally flooded by shallow marine transgressions followed by depositions of red sandstones and mudstones during the Mesozoic era.

questions.questionText: The extensive swamps that existed in tropical areas during the Mesozoic era later became rich deposits of:
questions.explanation: Tropical areas were dominated by extensive swamps which later became rich coal deposits.

questions.questionText: The development of volcanic mountain ranges in western North America was initiated by igneous activities during the:
questions.explanation: Igneous activities had initiated also the development of volcanic mountain ranges in western North America during the mid-Mesozoic era, simultaneous with the splitting of Pangaea.

questions.questionText: The distribution of water in the Earth's hydrosphere shows that the largest percentage of fresh water is stored in:
questions.explanation:
Oceans account for over 97% of water.

Of the remaining freshwater, Glaciers and polar ice caps contain just greater than 2%, while groundwater contains about 0.6% (which is 36 times more than in lakes and rivers combined).

questions.questionText: What is the key characteristic of the Mid-Ordovician Period (458 Ma) in terms of continental configuration?
options: The existence of four major continents: Gondwana, Baltica, Siberia, and Laurasia
The final separation of the present-day continents
questions.explanation: Four major continents (Gondwana, Baltica, Siberia, and Laurasia) came into being during 458 Ma (in the mid-Ordovician Period).

questions.questionText: What is the average depth of the Pacific Ocean basin?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean has an average depth of 4,028 meters.

questions.questionText: Which country is NOT listed among the main countries of North America in the textbook?
questions.explanation:
The main countries of North America are three (USA, Canada & Mexico).

Panama is part of Central America, which is the link to South America.

questions.questionText: The process of 'Continental Drift' and the theory of 'Sea-floor spreading' are two key mechanisms associated with which general concept?
options: The changing position of the continents and oceans
The formation of the Solar System
questions.explanation: Continental drift and Sea-floor spreading are keywords associated with the section on the changing position of the continents and oceans over geological times.

questions.questionText: Which ocean is the third-largest and is located between Africa, the Southern Ocean, Asia, and Australia?
questions.explanation:
The Indian Ocean is the world’s third-largest ocean (68,566,000 square kilometers). 

It is located in the area between Africa, the Southern Ocean, Asia, and Australia.

questions.questionText: The highest mountains (Himalayas) are found on which continent?
questions.explanation: Asia has the highest mountains (Himalayas).

questions.questionText: What separates the continents of Europe and Africa?
questions.explanation: Europe is bounded by the Atlantic and Arctic oceans and by the Mediterranean Sea in the south (separating it from Africa).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the life forms that evolved during the Paleozoic era?
questions.explanation:
Trilobites and shelled animals were common in the Paleozoic era, and the Devonian period was the age of fish.
Dinosaurs, however, dominated the subsequent Mesozoic era.

questions.questionText: What is the significance of the North American continent starting to develop from the assemblage of rocks at about 306 Ma (late Carboniferous period)?
options: It marked the start of the Cenozoic era
It preceded the break-up of Pangaea
It was part of the final assemblage that led to the Supercontinent (Pangaea)
It was the first major continent to form
questions.explanation:
At about 306 Ma (in the late Carboniferous period) the North American continent started to develop from the assemblage of rocks.
By then, the Supercontinent (Pangaea) had come into being at about 255 -210 Ma.

questions.questionText: The ice age primarily occurred during which epoch?
questions.explanation: The Ice Age occurred during the Pleistocene epoch (0.01 – 1.6 Ma).

questions.questionText: Early hominids appeared during which epoch of the Cenozoic Era?
questions.explanation: Early Hominids appeared during the Pliocene epoch (1.6 – 5.3 Ma).

questions.questionText: Which ocean is known for having a significant historical importance due to the Northwest Passage and the Northern Sea route being areas of trade and exploration?
questions.explanation: The Northwest Passage and the Northern Sea route have historically been important areas of trade and exploration in the Arctic Ocean.

questions.questionText: The final stage of continental break-up and the continents reaching their present form occurred after the Tertiary Period, in the:
questions.explanation: Continental break-up progressively continued during the Tertiary period; the Earth’s continents have then retained their present position during the Quaternary.

questions.questionText: What is the average depth of the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: The average depth of the Atlantic Ocean is 3,926 meters.

questions.questionText: The term 'mid-oceanic' ridge is a feature primarily associated with which of the following processes?
questions.explanation: 'mid-oceanic' ridge is a keyword listed under the formation and changing position of continents, as it is a key feature of sea-floor spreading.

questions.questionText: Which ocean extends from the coast of Antarctica to 60 degrees south latitude?
questions.explanation: The Southern Ocean extends from the coast of Antarctica to 60 degrees south latitude.

questions.questionText: The deepest point in the Southern Ocean is located in the south end of the:
questions.explanation: The deepest point in the Southern Ocean is in the south end of the South Sandwich Trench.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is considered one of the shallow seas of the Atlantic Ocean basin?
questions.explanation: The North Sea is explicitly listed as a shallow sea found in the Atlantic Ocean basin.

questions.questionText: The collision of which two continents closed the Iapetus Sea, preceding the formation of pre-Pangaea?
questions.explanation: The Laurasia continent collided with the Baltica and closed the Iapetus Sea during the mid-Silurian.

questions.questionText: The Mesozoic era is also called the era of 'middle life'. The time span for this era was:
questions.explanation: The Mesozoic era marked the time from 250-70 Ma.

questions.questionText: Which continent is home to the industrial revolution and is the second smallest continent in the world?
questions.explanation: Europe is the second smallest continent in the world, and home of the industrial revolution.

questions.questionText: The existence of extensive swamps in tropical areas during the Mesozoic era indicates a climate that was likely:
questions.explanation: Extensive swamps, which later formed coal deposits, suggest a warm and moist climate suitable for large-scale vegetation growth in the tropical areas during the Mesozoic era.

questions.questionText: The initial formation of the Earth is attributed to processes similar to the creation of other planets and the entire development of the:
questions.explanation: The formation of the Earth is attributed similar to the creation of other companion planets and the entire development of the Solar System.

questions.questionText: What is the land-to-ocean ratio in the Northern Hemisphere?
questions.explanation: In the Northern Hemisphere, the ratio of land to ocean is about 1:1.5.

questions.questionText: Which of the following continents has the largest part of its landmass situated north of the equator?
questions.explanation:
The equator divides Africa into two parts.

But the largest part of the continent is found north of the equator.

questions.questionText: The longest north-south extending mountain range, the Andes Mountains, is a key feature of:
questions.explanation: The north-south extending longest mountain (Andes Mt.) is found in South America.

questions.questionText: What is the average depth of the Southern Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Southern Ocean has an average depth ranging from 4,000 to 5,000 meters.

questions.questionText: The geological timescale establishes the sequence of events based on Eons, Eras, Periods, and Epochs. What is the broadest division of geological time?
questions.explanation: The Geological Timescale is divided into Eons (the largest division), which are subdivided into Eras, which are further divided into Periods, and then Epochs.

questions.questionText: The Cenozoic era is divided into two periods: the Paleogene and the:
questions.explanation: The Cenozoic Era is composed of the Paleogene and Neogene Periods (and the Quaternary Period).

questions.questionText: What is the geological time span of the Quaternary Period, which is a division of the Cenozoic Era?
questions.explanation: The Quaternary Period spans the time from the Present – 1.6 Ma, including the Holocene and Pleistocene epochs.
